newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Forrestania says has big nickel show.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Forrestania says has big nickel show.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Thursday that it had found large high grade nickel intercepts at its Maggie Hays deposit.

It said grades for the entire mineralised zone should be in the 2.0 percent to 2.5 percent nickel range and the intercepts found were amoung the best recorded in the exploration history of the Australian nickel industry.

"Two recent holes returned 50 metres at 2.02 percent nickel (including 6.9 metres of massive sulphides at a grade of 5.17 percent nickel) and 41.2 metres at 1.82 percent nickel (including 5.05 metres of massive sulphides at a grade of 4.66 percent nickel)," Forrestania said.

"A third hole currently being drilled has encountered a mineralised zone of 33.7 metres including 7.74 metres of massive sulphides," it said, adding that grades for this hole should be in the 2.0 percent to 2.5 percent range.
Forrestania Managing Director Barry Eldridge said the results demonstrated the enormous potential of the Maggie Hays orebody.
The orebody is contained within the Lake Johnston Joint Venture, which is 50 percent owned by Forrestania and 50 percent owned by South Africa's Gencor Ltd.

"The partners have accelerated work on the project and are spending A$8.7 million during the current financial year with the intention of commencing a bankable feasibility study in the September 1997 quarter," Forrestania said.
"Maggie Hays is shaping up as a world-class orebody and we are moving ahead as quickly as possible with development on a number of fronts," Eldridge said.
Gencor owns the BioNIC process, a bacterial method of extracting nickel and gold from sulphide ores.
